subject: Performance discovery — warmup/script handover & test window options
content:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Alvarez <sara@clearview.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Performance discovery — warmup/script handover & test window options

Hi Sara — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can align on the customer-led run: 

Summary of agreed targets (please confirm):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end (client request → first token) target <= 300ms for single-turn generation under production prompt sizes.
- Throughput: sustained 120 requests/sec to the primary endpoint (streaming responses allowed).
- Concurrency: support up to 200 concurrent sessions with streaming enabled (typical user pattern: 1–3 simultaneous SSE connections per heavy user).
- Streaming requirements: each streaming session will send a prompt and keep an open connection for token delivery; average generated token payload ~1.2k tokens per response.

What Redwood will provide before your run:
- Test account + ephemeral API token (instructions attached: redwood-test-account-instructions.pdf).
- A recommended warmup/runbook with ramp/soak phases and cache prefill steps (attached: warmup-runbook.md).
- A Locust handoff template (attached: locust-handoff-template.yaml) with two modes: HTTP POST for single-shot generation and an SSE client for streaming.
- IP ranges for inbound allowlist to permit Clearview's runners to reach our private test endpoints — see IP block list in my follow-up below.

Questions for you (please reply inline):
1) Where will you run your runners from (region/ASNs)? You mentioned AWS us-east-1 — can you confirm whether the runners will use ephemeral IPs or a NAT/Elastic IP pool?
2) Do you need support for long-lived streaming connections (we can bump idle timeouts to 25m for the window if required)?
3) Can you share one or two sample payloads (or approximate token sizes) so the Locust template can emulate your traffic distribution?

Proposed scheduling options:
- Dry run (short probe + runbook rehearsal): Tue Jan 19, 09:00–10:00 PT
- Full customer-led test window (ramp + 90-minute soak + validation): Wed Jan 20, 09:00–12:00 PT

If those windows work, Ben and Soojin will be on standby for the dry run and full window respectively.

Thanks — I’ll wait for the answers on IPs and sample payloads and will email the ephemeral token once we confirm the dry-run timing.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Sara Alvarez <sara@clearview.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@clearview.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 11:07:18 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance discovery — warmup/script handover & test window options

Neha — thanks, this is great. A couple quick answers and requests: 

1) Runners
We will run the Locust/synthetic traffic from AWS us-east-1. We have a small fleet behind an Elastic IP pool (we can provide exact EIPs). If you can confirm the IPs we should allowlist that would be ideal.

2) Streaming
We do need true streaming support (server-sent events or chunked HTTP). Our UX keeps connections open while the user composes follow-ups; typical connection durations during a session are 2–12 minutes. Having a 25m idle timeout will be helpful.

3) Payloads & tokens
I attached our ops IP list (clearview-ops-ips.txt). Sample payload: ~900 prompt tokens, ~1k generated tokens. We can provide sanitized JSON examples if you prefer.

4) Windows
We prefer Wed Jan 20, 09:00–12:00 PT for the full run but would like a short dry-run on Tue Jan 19, 08:30–09:00 PT to validate connectivity and auth.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Alvarez
SRE Lead, Clearview Analytics
Ops: ops@clearview.com

Sara / Neha — quick ops note from our side ahead of the dry run: 

Ephemeral credentials (for dry run):
- API key: REDWOOD-PROBE-XXXXXX (expires 24h after issuance) — do not use for production.
- Base URL: https://test-api.redwood.ai/clearview/v1/generate
- Streaming flag: enable_stream=true (for streaming endpoints)

IP ranges to allowlist on your side for inbound callbacks/metrics:
- 34.198.12.55/32
- 34.198.12.56/32
- 52.200.111.10/32
(These are our test egress IPs for the seeding window; we'll push the exact list again 24h before the run.)

Recommended warmup phases (short):
1) Cache prefill (10–15m): run small-batch prompts to warm KV/prefix caches (we include examples in warmup-runbook.md).
2) Ramp (15m): linear ramp to target concurrency.
3) Soak (60–90m): sustain target throughput; collect p50/p95/p99 and token delivery timelines.
4) Cooldown (10m): step down traffic and validate error rates.

Observability hooks we’ll enable for the window:
- Token-level latency tracing for a sampled 1% of requests.
- Per-route cost and latency dashboards shared with the Clearview team.
- Streaming buffer metrics (if any stalls occur we’ll correlate with network).

Attachments sent: warmup-runbook.md (run phases and curl examples). I’ll create the ephemeral key and post to you privately once you confirm the dry run time.

—Ben
Ben Carter
